audit.costly_failure: The ledger repeatedly found that a receipt merely refreshed in the same session could still prove a different source tree; freshness alone did not bind evidence to the candidate.
audit.evidence: Ledger fact in my words: the costly failure was inherited or unrelated verification evidence accepted after a source change. The untested boundary was receipt provenance rather than receipt age. The distinguishing input is a valid-format receipt whose digest was made before agent.py changes, then checked after that change.

matrix.requirement: A verification receipt is accepted for exactly the candidate whose digest it records.
matrix.input: A temporary workspace containing agent.py version 1 and a receipt generated from its digest, with the receipt excluded from hashing.
matrix.expected: verification_problems returns no problems; updating the receipt itself does not create a self-reference mismatch.
matrix.observed: 1 passed in 0.02s; the test wrote a matching receipt and observed an empty problem tuple.

matrix.requirement: A receipt from an earlier source tree must reject a later source edit even when all required receipt fields remain present.
matrix.input: The same temporary workspace after changing agent.py from version 1 to version 2 without rewriting candidate_digest.
matrix.expected: verification_problems returns exactly memories/verification.json.candidate_digest does not match the current candidate.
matrix.observed: 1 passed in 0.02s; the adversarial mutation produced the asserted exact mismatch message.

matrix.requirement: Existing verification and publication checks remain usable with the new required binding.
matrix.input: The full repository test suite after candidate-digest validation and prompt changes.
